anchors.1: Unrelated, unintelligible, empty, or only a greeting/general request for help.
anchors.2: Some topic words overlap, but the response addresses a different question.
anchors.3: Addresses the requested topic through an acknowledgement, offer or generic advice, without a direct answer.
anchors.4: Directly addresses the question, with a minor detour or unnecessary clarification.
anchors.5: Direct, focused answer to the actual question; an explicit context-appropriate inability to determine the answer also qualifies.

support.label: Factual support

anchors.1: Major contradiction, invented completed lookup/action, or central unsupported factual assertion.
anchors.2: A material claim goes beyond the context, such as unestablished current availability or an invented event.
anchors.3: Mostly supported facts with a smaller unsupported detail or overstatement.
anchors.4: All material claims supported, with a minor imprecision that does not change the answer.
anchors.5: All material claims faithfully supported by the supplied context, with appropriate qualification.

support.not_applicable: Use null when there are no material factual assertions, including pure offers, greetings or an honest statement of insufficient context. Do not give these responses a vacuous 5.

anchors.1: Does not answer; off-topic/greeting/empty, or substantively wrong/fabricated.
anchors.2: Relevant offer or generic advice without a substantive answer; major missing available information.
anchors.3: Useful partial answer, but an important available point or qualification is missing.
anchors.4: Substantially answers the question using available evidence; minor omission or excess detail.
anchors.5: Complete, useful answer appropriate to the available context and question. With insufficient context, explicitly identifies that limit and avoids inventing unavailable facts.

literature.title: G-Eval
literature.use: Explicit task criteria and evaluation steps; aspect scores. This adaptation does not reproduce probability-weighted G-Eval scoring.

literature.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
literature.use: Reference-guided single-answer assessment, bias controls and prompt-order sensitivity checks; human agreement is not assumed for this local judge.

literature.title: Prometheus 2
literature.use: Criterion-specific 1–5 anchors, reference answers and feedback before ratings. The actual model here is Qwen3, not Prometheus.
